chunks: And that which was narrated - Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother (peace be upon him) said:

I asked him about a man who forgot the obligatory Tawaf until he returned to his country and had intercourse with women; what should he do? He said: 'He sends a Hady (sacrificial animal); if he left it during Hajj, he sends it during Hajj, and if he left it during Umrah, he sends it during Umrah, and he appoints someone to perform the Tawaf on his behalf for what he left of his Tawaf.'

So it is applicable to the Tawaf of the women (Umrah), because whoever leaves the Tawaf of the women (Umrah) forgetfully, it is permissible for him to appoint another in his place for his Tawaf, and it is not permissible for him to do so in the Tawaf of Hajj; so there is no contradiction between the two narrations.
That which indicates what we mentioned is that which was narrated:

key_terms.طَوَافُ النِّسَاءِ: Tawaf of Umrah (literally: Tawaf of the women)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who forgets the obligatory Tawaf and returns home?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies the expiation for a pilgrim who forgets the obligatory Tawaf and returns home, ruling that he must send a sacrificial animal (Hady) and appoint a proxy to perform the missed circumambulation. This ruling specifically applies to the Tawaf of Umrah, distinguishing it from the Tawaf of Hajj where proxy performance is generally not permitted for the forgetful, thereby resolving apparent contradictions in other narrations. The emphasis on sending the Hady separately highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the sacrificial offering remains a distinct obligation even when the ritual act is performed by a deputy.
